assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (incretin action, proglucagon processing, glucose-dependent insulin secretion, appetite effects) led to a drug class that has changed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity and shows cardiovascular and renal benefit. Combines clear physiological discovery with transformative, durable clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: Holst and Drucker made decisive physiological and mechanistic contributions; Knudsen led the design of long-acting acylated GLP-1 analogues (liraglutide, semaglutide). Mojsov's contribution to identifying the active GLP-1 peptide is real, and others outside the credited list (e.g. Habener) may also have claims; a three-person split is contested.
assessment.maturity: Mature: decades of confirmation, large randomised outcome trials, global clinical use. Timing is strong given scale of impact.
uncertainties: Fair allocation among Drucker, Holst, Mojsov and Knudsen is unresolved and I have not independently verified the details of the priority dispute.
Whether the committee prefers recognising the physiology or the drug development.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produce durable remissions in refractory B-cell leukaemias and lymphomas, and are now extending to myeloma and autoimmune disease. Conceptually original and clinically transformative.
assessment.attribution: Rosenberg pioneered adoptive T-cell therapy and early gene-modified T cells and CAR trials; Sadelain developed CD28 co-stimulated CARs; June led the clinical translation of 4-1BB CARs (CTL019). Eshhar and others are not on this list, which constrains the configuration.
assessment.maturity: Approved products since 2017 with years of follow-up; durability and safety (CRS, neurotoxicity, secondary malignancy) are better defined, and expansion into other diseases is ongoing.
uncertainties: Priority among early CAR designers (not all in the credited list) is only partly captured.
Long-term safety and efficacy outside haematologic cancers remain unsettled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showed TNF to be a dominant driver of cytokine cascades in rheumatoid synovium and that its blockade yields clinical benefit; this established anti-cytokine therapy and transformed inflammatory disease care across RA, IBD, psoriasis and spondyloarthritis.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini's translational line from synovial cytokine biology to clinical proof of concept is clear and a natural two-person configuration; other contributors (e.g. Kollias, Cerami, Vilcek) may be raised.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: more than two decades of clinical use, biosimilars, extensive confirmation. Recognition is arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Allocation relative to those who first characterised TNF biology and developed the antibodies is debated.
Recognised as translational medicine rather than a single mechanistic discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle HPV vaccines prevent persistent infection and cervical precancer, and population data show large declines in cervical disease. Strong preventive-medicine and cancer-prevention impact following on the HPV-cancer link already recognised.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed L1 VLPs at NCI; Frazer (with Zhou Jian, deceased) developed the VLP approach independently. Three living names form a plausible configuration; Zhou's contribution and parallel industry work complicate fairness.
assessment.maturity: Mature: licensed since 2006, with real-world effectiveness evidence including cervical cancer incidence reductions in vaccinated cohorts.
uncertainties: Priority dispute and the role of the deceased co-inventor are unresolved.
Long-term cancer-endpoint data are still maturing in many populations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeting the BCR-ABL kinase with imatinib turned CML from a fatal into a chronic condition and validated targeted cancer therapy as a paradigm; the work also revealed resistance mechanisms that guided next-generation inhibitors.
assessment.attribution: Lydon led the discovery of the compound, Druker the clinical proof and development, Sawyers the resistance mechanism and second-generation inhibitor strategy. Ties to earlier BCR-ABL discovery (Rowley, Witte, others) leave the boundary of the prize partly open.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: long-term survival data show durable benefit, and the concept has been replicated across kinase-driven cancers.
uncertainties: Whether the foundational oncogene discoveries make this a drug-development prize in the committee's view.
Whether Sawyers or the earlier genetics should be included.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway defined how cytosolic DNA triggers innate immunity, with implications for infection, autoimmunity, interferonopathies, and cancer immunity. A clear mechanistic discovery that opened a broad field.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the cGAMP second messenger; Barber identified STING. Sun, Wu and Ishikawa are co-discoverers on specific steps, so a two-person configuration leaves out some contributors.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature: mechanism well established and reproduced, but therapeutic translation (STING agonists and inhibitors) has yet to deliver clear approved benefit.
uncertainties: Attribution among the cGAS, cGAMP and STING discoveries is partly shared.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Human genetics (gain-of-function mutations in familial hypercholesterolaemia and loss-of-function variants with low LDL-C) identified PCSK9 as a causal target, and led quickly to antibodies and siRNA that lower LDL cholesterol and cardiovascular events. A model of genetics-to-therapy.
assessment.attribution: Abifadel, Boileau and colleagues linked PCSK9 mutations to FH; Seidah characterised the proprotein convertase; Hobbs and Cohen showed protective loss-of-function variants and mechanism. Five credited names must be reduced to three, which risks an unfair omission of Cohen or Boileau.
assessment.maturity: Mature enough: approved drugs, outcome trial (FOURIER, ODYSSEY) benefit; cholesterol lowering itself is already recognised by earlier prizes.
uncertainties: Fair three-person selection from five contributors is unresolved.
Incremental to earlier statin and LDL receptor recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics allows causal, cell-type-specific control of neural activity with light and has become a standard tool across neuroscience, with first therapeutic applications in vision restoration. Originality and methodological influence are very high.
assessment.attribution: Nagel, Hegemann and Bamberg characterised channelrhodopsin; Deisseroth and Boyden established its use in neurons; Miesenböck made an earlier genetically targeted photoactivation approach. Six credited names exceed the three-person limit, so attribution is the main obstacle.
assessment.maturity: Mature as a tool with extensive independent confirmation; clinical translation is early.
uncertainties: Allocation among at least six contributors, including Bamberg and Miesenböck, is unresolved.
Primary impact is on research method rather than medicine.
